evidence.relation: crowding unwind -> continued short-term underperformance of AI index

evidence.relation: duration/valuation analogy -> long-run upside, weak signal for 90-day horizon

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — AI Bubble Burst. Is it Finally Over? (2026-07-31)
evidence.claim: Nasdaq top-component forward PE is about 22x against about 60x in 2000, the index is about 5% undervalued against 91% overvalued in 2000, and the AI boom is 3.6 years old and +157% against the dot-com's 5.3 years and +1,092%.
evidence.relation: A dot-com analog with much lower valuations and gains so far suggests the index is not at a bubble top and could rise further, perhaps 1-1.7 years, before a final burst.

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — The S&P 500 Just Hit 7,800. Can It Go Higher, or Is This the Top? (2026-08-17)
evidence.claim: The Nasdaq 100 is up 19.2% YTD with the short-term and medium-term moving-average trends aligned upward.
evidence.relation: An aligned multi-timeframe uptrend (20 EMA above 40 EMA, 50 SMA above a rising 150 SMA) historically favors continued upward momentum, and the March dip did not break the medium-term trend.

resolution: Short-term rotation-out evidence (qqq-1) vs fundamental-intact evidence (qqq-3) genuinely conflict; both kept. Resolution: rotation is a flow phenomenon (weeks), fundamentals a valuation phenomenon (quarters). For the 90-day view the flow leg dominates while Fed-hike odds (already in prior) suppress multiples — posterior stays near neutral, slightly above the pre-evidence market wash because earnings breadth data is the strongest verified fact in the set.
